field_glossary.backend_ladder: Per-backend outcome of the kernel-agent dispatch. ``produced_artifact=false`` across all rows is the dominant signal that the entire ladder failed for this kernel.
field_glossary.bandwidth: Per-case ``bytes`` / ``algbw_gbps`` / ``busbw_gbps`` from the final bench. Latency alone cannot separate a faster transfer from a cheaper barrier; bus bandwidth against the fabric peak says which one a kept kernel bought, and which regime still has headroom.
field_glossary.bound_type: Whether the kernel is limited by memory bandwidth (memory-bound) or compute (compute-bound).
field_glossary.collective_attempt_id: Stable identity for one collective campaign, used to deduplicate resumed or salvaged attempts across a session.
field_glossary.collective_op: The collective primitive that was optimized: ``all_reduce``, ``reduce_scatter`` or ``all_gather``.
field_glossary.compile_passed: True only if at least one backend in the ladder produced a usable patch. False means the whole backend ladder failed to produce any compiled artifact.
field_glossary.e2e_gain_pct: End-to-end throughput delta measured by the integrate gate. This, not micro_speedup, decides whether a collective KEEP is adopted.
field_glossary.efficiency_pct: Achieved throughput as a percentage of the kernel's roofline peak for its bound_type. Lower = more headroom to gain.
field_glossary.gpu_pct: Share of total GPU time spent in this kernel (kernel_duration / total_gpu_duration). Higher = more impactful to optimize.
field_glossary.lane: Which optimization lane produced the row. ``collective`` rows come from the multi-GPU comm lane and carry no roofline geometry, so efficiency_pct / bound_type / arithmetic_intensity stay null.
field_glossary.salvaged: True when the validated best was recovered from the campaign sidecar after the wrapper timed out, rather than returned by a clean exit.
field_glossary.speedup_basis: Whether the row's headline number was validated end to end (``e2e``) or is a microbenchmark ratio only. A collective's microbenchmark routinely overstates its end-to-end worth, so treat ``microbenchmark`` rows as unproven.
field_glossary.world_size: Rank count the collective was measured across; the lane requires it to match the run's TP width.

proposal_set.name: gdn-ssm-state-bf16
proposal_set.reason: config.json declares text_config.mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' and vLLM's Qwen3_5ForConditionalGenerationConfig.verify_and_update_config copies that straight into cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype when it is 'auto' (model_executor/models/config.py:781-805). So the GDN recurrent state cache is fp32. Per request per decode step the 48 linear-attn layers read+write a [48 v-heads,128k,128v] state = 786KB/layer, ~37.8MB read + ~37.8MB write = ~75MB of HBM traffic, vs ~12MB of KV for the 16 full-attn layers at seq 2k. At conc=64 that is ~4.8GB/step against ~3.9TB/s peak (~1.2ms of pure state movement per ~28ms step, 10-20% of the decode step) and it scales with concurrency while GEMM time does not. bf16 halves the state bytes; INT8 W8A8 already halves the weight-side traffic, so state bandwidth is proportionally MORE dominant here than in a bf16 run. Baseline steady-state decode is 729 tok/s vs 512.5 reported, so decode-side wins translate almost 1:1. Secondary effect confirmed in the log: 'Setting attention block size to 784 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size' - the 784-token attention block is derived from the mamba page, so halving the state shrinks that forced page inflation and the associated fragmentation.

proposal_set.name: decoder-for-triton-attn-backend
proposal_set.reason: The selector logged 'Found incompatible backend(s) [TURBOQUANT] with AttentionType.DECODER. Overriding with ROCM_ATTN out of potential backends: [ROCM_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN]' - so ROCM_ATTN was picked by elimination, not by preference, and TRITON_ATTN is the other already-validated-compatible candidate. ROCM_ATTN implements prefill+decode in one fused Triton kernel, and its own module logged 'Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation' (chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:463) - the plain chunked-prefill-paged-decode path, which is markedly weaker than a flash-style split prefill kernel at hd=256 / 24Q-4KV heads. That matters a lot here: from the baseline log, prefill windows run 1252-1843 prompt tok/s while generation in the SAME window collapses to 27-278 tok/s, i.e. prefill and decode are essentially serialized; ~38.5s of prefill per 133s wave (~29% of wall clock) is spent on a kernel that fell back. head_dim=256 is inside ROCM_ATTN's and TRITON_ATTN's supported head sizes, so this is a like-for-like backend swap with no shape risk. Not the AITER FA path that platform law 11 rules out for hd256 - that would need VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA/UNIFIED_ATTENTION and is explicitly a known dead end; this proposal does not touch it.

proposal_set.name: prefill-batch-4096
proposal_set.reason: max_num_batched_tokens is not set in the base recipe, so it is the SchedulerConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS = 2048 (config/scheduler.py:42,49). Output throughput is bounded by wall clock, and prefill is ~29% of it (327680 input tokens at ~1700-1843 tok/s peak = ~38.5s per 5-wave cycle vs ~94.5s of decode at the 92.3ms median ITL). Raising the per-step token budget to 4096 lets 3-4 1024-token prefills share one step instead of ~2, which on CDNA2 lifts the attention/GEMM shapes out of the skinny regime and amortises the per-step fixed cost (64 GDN state reads/writes + graph replay) that is otherwise paid once per prefill chunk. Cheapest-to-interpret complement to the two kernel-side proposals: it attacks prefill throughput directly rather than decode. Note the current compile range endpoint is 2048, so this adds a second dynamo compile range (longer warmup, covered by the existing compile cache); if the run shows TPOT mean degrading while TTFT improves, revert.

proposal_set.name: no-prefix-cache-packed-decode
proposal_set.reason: ATOMIC: both halves are required. new_findings.what: GDN state dtype: the fp32 is declarative, not required, and narrowing the store does not change the recurrence arithmetic. Verified in the Triton decode kernels actually used ('GDN decode kernel: triton'): the accumulator is created fp32 (b_h = tl.zeros([BV,BK], dtype=tl.float32)), the state is upcast on load (tl.load(p_h0).to(tl.float32)) and requantized on store (tl.store(p_ht, b_h.to(p_ht.dtype.element_ty))). There is no separate internal fp32 state buffer, so --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 changes exactly one bf16 round-trip of S per decoded token and nothing else. Per-step HBM traffic for the state is ~0.52 MB vs ~1.05 MB per token per layer (HV_local=8, K=V=128) across the 48 linear-attn layers - the single largest decode-side stream at conc=64. Kernel grid/tiling is head-driven and block-size independent, so no grid regression. The 784-token attention block size is inflated purely to match the fp32 mamba page size, so halving it also relieves the block-size mismatch on the 16 full-attn layers.

The GDN recurrent state is fp32 only because the checkpoint declares mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' and vLLM auto-adopts it - not because a kernel needs it. The state cache is the largest per-step HBM stream at conc=64 (~0.52 vs ~1.05 MB per token per layer over 48 linear-attn layers), and decode is bandwidth-bound at ~729 tok/s, so halving it is the biggest bandwidth lever left. I verified in the exact Triton decode kernels this run uses that the accumulator is created fp32, the state is upcast on load and requantized on store, and there is no internal fp32 state buffer - so bf16 narrows only the per-token store->load round-trip and cannot change the recurrence arithmetic. Side benefit: the 784-token attention block size exists only to match the fp32 mamba page size, so this also relieves that inflation on the 16 full-attn layers.

Atomic: --mamba-cache-mode all on its own OOMed the KV cache profile at 35.92 GiB against 32.12 GiB available (round 20260915T115135Z-37d175d3), but this flag pair fixes that exact cause. 'align' allocates one GDN state page per 784-token block (8x the states needed and ~87% of the block bytes wasted); 'all' allocates one state per sliding window, which is what lets --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 collapse the page size to a single 16B fp16 vector. The combination is the documented pairing in config/cache.py:130-134, it shrinks rather than grows the footprint, and the two flags only make sense together - splitting them reproduces the two prior failures. Kept 4th because the prior 'all' attempt cost 49% prefill throughput.

Cheap, accuracy-neutral A/B against the single most contested lever on this stack, and worth one slot purely because the round-1 verdict is provably not reproducible. The earlier session's '--speculative-config {method:mtp...}' failed with 'model must have mtp_num_hidden_layers and num_speculative_tokens to use MTP', so the engine never started and never measured anything; the standalone flag routes through get_num_speculative_tokens() instead and is exactly the path that session's own suggestion asked for. On this stack --num-speculative-steps only starts with mamba_cache_mode='align', which is already the baseline, so the config is valid as-is. If it launches and does not move the needle, that closes MTP for this benchmark with a real number instead of a startup crash; it will most likely fail fast (no draft weight loaded, or the fork's 'ssm state dtype float32 is not compatible with MTP' gate).

Exploratory, last, and gated on the accuracy margin - but the mechanism is not the usual 'no shared prefixes' argument, which does not apply here. The run REPORTS a 38-76% prefix cache hit rate on 320 random-token prompts, i.e. real reuse exists, and prefix caching is precisely what forces mamba_cache_mode='align' and the 784-token attention block (server.log:14,42). Dropping it frees the per-step block-hash / free-match machinery on the EngineCore critical path and lets the block size be chosen by the attention layers alone; it also removes the state-page churn on eviction, which is the known pathological case for 'align' and which no proposal addresses today. Two risks the bench must watch: a hit-rate loss can raise TTFT enough to cut mean TTFT from 3.8s to ~1.0s, and the 604320:169248 input:output ratio means an unshared prompt token costs more compute than an output token earns.
